```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk[["set"]](echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(deSolve)
library(EpiEstim)
```

## 1. SEIR Model with Random Noise in Transmission
Here we add an Exposed (`E`) compartment for the latent period (`gamma = 1/5` days) and draw `beta` from a normal distribution at each step to mimic noisy outbreak data.

```{r seir-noisy}
SEIR_model <- function(t, state, parameters) {
  with(as.list(c(state, parameters)), {
    P <- (S + E + I + R)
    
    # Unused helper variables from class exploration
    rand <- max(rnorm(1, I, 2), 0)
    P_aux <- S + E + rand + R
    
    # Stochastic force of infection (beta fluctuates randomly around 0.35)
    lam <- max(rnorm(1, parameters['beta'], 5e-1), 0) * I / P

    # SEIR ODEs with vital dynamics (mu)
    dS <- mu * P - mu * S - lam * S   
    dE <- lam * S - gamma * E - mu * E
    dI <- gamma * E - tau * I - mu * I 
    dR <- tau * I - mu * R
    
    list(c(dS, dE, dI, dR))
  }) 
}

# Initial conditions (P = 999, 1 initial infectious case)
initP <- 999
initE <- 0
initI <- 1 
initR <- 0 
initS <- initP - initI - initR - initE
istate <- c(S = initS, E = initE, I = initI, R = initR)

# Parameters (5-day latent period, 10-day infectious period)
parameters <- c(
  mu = (1 / (50 * 52 * 7)),    
  beta = 0.35,              
  gamma = 1 / 5,          
  tau = 1 / 10            
)

# Exact R0 formula for SEIR with vital dynamics
R0 <- parameters["beta"] * parameters["gamma"] /
  ((parameters["gamma"] + parameters["mu"]) * (parameters["tau"] + parameters["mu"]))
R0

# Simulate for 365 days with fine time steps (0.01 days)
time_start <- 0
time_stop <- 365 
deltat <- 0.01
tps <- seq(time_start, time_stop, by = deltat)

out <- deSolve::ode(y = istate, times = tps, func = SEIR_model, parms = parameters) 
Flu2009 <- as.data.frame(out)

# Plot all 4 compartments and check that total population N remains constant
plot(out)
N <- rowSums(Flu2009[, 2:5])
plot(N, type = "l", ylab = "Total Population (N)", xlab = "Step")
```

## 2. Estimating Time-Varying Rt with `EpiEstim`
Next, we compute daily incidence (`gamma * E`), filter to whole days, estimate $R_t$ using `EpiEstim`, and compare the estimate (blue) against the true model $R_t = R_0 \cdot S/N$ (red).

```{r epiestim-rt}
# Daily incidence = rate of individuals transitioning from E to I
Flu2009[["incidence"]] <- parameters["gamma"] * Flu2009[["E"]]

# Filter indices corresponding to exact integer days (t = 0, 1, 2, ...)
ww <- which(Flu2009[["time"]] %% 1 == 0.0)

# Estimate Rt from daily incidence using a parametric serial interval
res_parametric_si <- estimate_R(
  abs(Flu2009[["incidence"]][ww]), 
  method = "parametric_si", 
  config = make_config(list(mean_si = 2.5, std_si = 1.5))
) 
plot(res_parametric_si, legend = FALSE)

# Calculate theoretical Rt directly from the simulation's susceptible fraction
Rt <- R0 * Flu2009[["S"]] / (Flu2009[["S"]] + Flu2009[["E"]] + Flu2009[["I"]] + Flu2009[["R"]])

# Compare true Rt (red) vs EpiEstim estimate (blue) for the first 100 days
plot(Rt[ww], type = "l", col = "red", lwd = 2, ylim = c(0, 3), ylab = "Rt", xlab = "Time (days)")
lines(res_parametric_si[["R"]][["Mean(R)"]][1:100], col = "blue", lwd = 2)
legend("topright", legend = c("True Simulated Rt", "EpiEstim Mean(R)"), col = c("red", "blue"), lwd = 2)
```

## 3. Method of Stages: 4-Stage Infectious Period (`SEIR_model_4n`)
Here, `I` is split into 4 sequential compartments (`I1` to `I4`), each moving at rate `4 * tau`. This keeps the mean infectious period at 10 days while replacing the exponential distribution with a tighter Erlang (Gamma) distribution.

```{r seir-4stages}
SEIR_model_4n <- function(t, state, parameters) {
  with(as.list(c(state, parameters)), {
    P <- (S + E + I1 + I2 + I3 + I4 + R)
    n <- 4
    lam <- rnorm(1, parameters['beta'], 5e-3) * (I1 + I2 + I3 + I4) / P
    
    dS <- mu * P - mu * S - lam * S   
    dE <- lam * S - gamma * E - mu * E
    dI1 <- gamma * E - tau * n * I1 - mu * I1 
    dI2 <- tau * n * I1 - mu * I2 - tau * n * I2
    dI3 <- tau * n * I2 - mu * I3 - tau * n * I3
    dI4 <- tau * n * I3 - mu * I4 - tau * n * I4
    dR <- n * tau * I4 - mu * R
    
    list(c(dS, dE, dI1, dI2, dI3, dI4, dR))
  }) 
}

# Initial conditions (1 case in each of I1..I4, so 4 total initial infectious cases)
initP <- 999
initE <- 0
initI1 <- 1 
initI2 <- 1 
initI3 <- 1 
initI4 <- 1 
initR <- 0 
initS <- initP - initI1 - initI2 - initI3 - initI4 - initR
istate4n <- c(S = initS, E = initE, I1 = initI1, I2 = initI2, I3 = initI3, I4 = initI4, R = initR)

out4n <- deSolve::ode(y = istate4n, times = tps, func = SEIR_model_4n, parms = parameters) 
Flu2009_4n <- as.data.frame(out4n)

plot(out4n)
```
